subject: HarborTrust RFP: vendor ecosystem mapping and subprocessor change-notice
messages:
From: Sam Klein <sam.klein@harbortrust.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@harbortrust.com
Date: Sat, 02 May 2026 09:14:00 -0400
Subject: RFP follow-up — vendor registry & change notification policy

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking our RFP. As part of our vendor risk assessment we need: a) a current list of all subprocessors (names, function, hosting region), b) your standard change-notice policy for additions/replacements of subprocessors, and c) assurances around primary cloud provider and any nested third parties (e.g., CDN, monitoring, analytics).

Please attach the registry and any policy language you can share. Two specific questions:
- What is your typical notification window for a non-emergency subprocessor change?
- How do you handle emergency replacements (time-to-notify, mitigations, temporary controls)?

We’re on a tight procurement timeline and would like those artifacts by COB Wednesday (2026-05-06). If there are items that require redaction (IP/price), flag them and we’ll coordinate.

Thanks,
Sam Klein
Senior Procurement Manager
HarborTrust Bank
procurement@harbortrust.com
(555) 212-0983

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Klein <sam.klein@harbortrust.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com, jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sat, 02 May 2026 12:08:00 -0400
Subject: RE: RFP follow-up — vendor registry & change notification policy

Sam —

Appreciate the clear ask. I’m attaching the current subprocessor registry and a consolidated data flow diagram for HarborTrust’s review. High-level answers below; detailed language and a change-notice exhibit are attached as a template.

Attachments (stubs):
- redwood_subprocessor_registry_20260502.csv (CSV, listing vendor name / role / country / SOC2 status / contractual data access)
- data_flow_diagram_v2.png (PNG, shows how customer content flows through Redwood services and key subprocessors)
- change_notice_template.docx (Word, proposed exhibit language for contract)

Quick answers:  
- Typical notice for planned (non-emergency) subprocessor additions/replacements: 30 calendar days prior to first processing event. Notice includes: new subprocessor name, purpose, locations, security certifications, and SOC2/other evidence where available.
- Emergency replacements: We commit to immediate notification (within 48 hours of the change) and will provide compensating controls and evidence within 15 calendar days. Emergency replacements are infrequent and reserved for outages/contractual terminations where continuity requires a fast swap; contract language allows temporary measures with customer approval where the change would materially alter processing of customer data.

Cloud provider assurances: Redwood’s primary cloud provider for hosted customers is AWS (multi-region). We use managed services and a small set of third-party providers for logging/monitoring and CDN. For each vendor in the registry we include the certification column (e.g., SOC2 Type II, ISO27001). We host customer data in region-specific clusters where required by contract.

If HarborTrust would like tighter SLAs around notification (e.g., 15-day planned notice) or additional evidence for any specific vendor (penetration test, supply-chain attestation), let me know and we’ll route through legal/security for a conversation.

CC’ing Neha (Security) and Jonas (Legal) to ensure the exhibit aligns to our standard contractual commitments.

Thanks — I can hop on a 30-minute call early next week if helpful.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Head of Partnerships, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com
Attachment: redwood_subprocessor_registry_20260502.csv (csv)
Attachment: data_flow_diagram_v2.png (png)
Attachment: change_notice_template.docx (docx)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Sam Klein <sam.klein@harbortrust.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sun, 03 May 2026 08:36:00 -0400
Subject: RE: RFP follow-up — vendor registry & change notification policy

Soojin / Sam —

Quick note from legal on the exhibit language: we should be explicit about the notification channels and the minimum evidence package we’ll provide for new subprocessors. Proposed edits to the template:
- Add requirement that planned notices are posted to the customer portal and emailed to the primary security contact simultaneously (so there’s an audit trail).
- For any new subprocessor that will have access to customer PII, Redwood will provide SOC2 report or equivalent within 15 calendar days of notice, and a summary of security controls mapped to HarborTrust’s control set (we can provide a control matrix excerpt).
- In emergency events, Redwood will: 1) notify within 48 hours, 2) provide mitigation steps immediately, and 3) deliver full evidence (SOC2/attestation/pen-test summary) within 15 calendar days.

Neha — please confirm the security evidence we can commit to under the standard enterprise agreement (SOC2 Type II and pen test summary are ok; full FTR logs or source-level artifacts are out-of-scope without additional legal agreement).

Sam — if those edits look reasonable I can prepare a redline and sign-off sheet. If HarborTrust requires changes beyond that (shorter notice windows, extra attestations) flag them and we’ll escalate.

-Jonas
General Counsel (acting)
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Klein <sam.klein@harbortrust.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com, jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sun, 03 May 2026 14:45:00 -0400
Subject: RE: RFP follow-up — vendor registry & change notification policy

Sam —

Following up with the consolidated package and suggested exhibit language attached. Per Jonas / Neha notes, highlights below:

- Planned subprocessor changes: 30-day email + portal notice to designated HarborTrust security contact (we propose: security@harbortrust.com).
- Emergency replacement: notify within 48 hours; mitigation steps within 72 hours; full evidence within 15 calendar days.
- Evidence we can provide by default: SOC2 Type II report, pen-test summary, vendor security questionnaire responses (where permitted by vendor NDA). We cannot provide vendor source code or raw customer logs without separate agreements.

Attachments (sent): redwood_subprocessor_registry_20260502.csv; data_flow_diagram_v2.png; change_notice_template.docx; DocuSign exhibit link: https://docusign.com/EXHIBIT-HTB-20260502

Next steps: 1) Review the attached exhibit and registry; 2) If acceptable, confirm whether HarborTrust wants the exhibit as an Attachable Exhibit or a contract Schedule (we can supply both formats via DocuSign); 3) Schedule a 30-minute call if you want to walk the registry row-by-row.

Would you like to schedule a call Monday or Tuesday morning (ET)?

Thanks,
Soojin
